_comment: Declared blind spots of the quality defence, as measured by scripts/quality_matrix.py.
This file is a registry, not a to-do list: tests/test_quality_matrix.py fails when the
measured set of holes differs from the set declared here, in EITHER direction. A new
blind spot therefore cannot land silently - it has to be written down with an exit
criterion first - and a hole that gets closed cannot stay here as decoration, because
an obsolete entry reads as an open one.
Fields: id = '<kind>:<name>' exactly as measured; opened = date the measurement found
it; exit = the concrete, checkable state that removes it; why = one line of context.
QUALITY_MATRIX.md must list every id in this file and no others.
An empty list is a measured state, not an aspiration: the same gate that fails on an
unregistered hole fails on a registered one the measurement no longer reproduces.

holes.exit: `.ci/seed-reach.txt` carries no `json_roundtrip` line, which happens when the seed named there is re-mined into a document one dialect accepts or moved to `fuzz/seeds/parse_json/`, whose target asserts on refusals; `cargo test -p pyrs-yaml-core --test seed_reach` is what reddens while the two disagree
holes.why: the target `continue`s when all three JSON dialects refuse, so the one seed named there replays clean while the round-trip invariant it was archived for is never asked of it

holes.exit: `.ci/seed-reach.txt` carries no `toml_roundtrip` line, reached by re-mining each named input into a document one TOML gate parses or moving it to `fuzz/seeds/parse_toml/`, where the refusal is the thing under test; the same `seed_reach` test holds the list and the measurement together
holes.why: the target skips its body when both the 1.1 and the 1.0 gate refuse, so the three seeds named there prove the refusal still stands and nothing about the note placement they were filed for

holes.exit: `.ci/seed-reach.txt` carries no `yaml_roundtrip` line, reached either by re-mining each named input into a document `parse(Schema::Core)` accepts or by moving it to a target that asserts on the refusal (`parse_yaml`, or `edit_yaml` once its script reaches the verbs); five of the seven became unreachable because a later ruling made the engine refuse duplicate-keyed documents, which is why they are registered rather than deleted
holes.why: `let Ok(node) = parse(text, Schema::Core) else { return }` is the target's first line, so a refused seed never reaches the idempotence assertion, yet the corpus total and the `former-crash-*` count still credit it as regression protection
